quote.author: VirtualElena
quote.name: Elena
quote.text:
one assumption i want to question about AI is that we'll eventually figure out the “best future” and then the remaining task will be getting everyone to agree to it. people want different things, and what they want can change. where more intelligence will help is in making those differences easier to accommodate.

nick bostrom's influence is worth revisiting on anthropic's ipo day. dario, like many of today’s most influential ai founders and researchers, read his work over a decade ago, and bostrom’s book superintelligence helped define questions the industry still faces. i'd like us to engage just as seriously with the possibilities bostrom explores in deep utopia, his subsequent book which asks what we do after we get superintelligence. some notes from my conversation with @eddylazzarin:

-superintelligence could make radically different versions of the “good life” possible. you might want a 200-year lifespan and a village where nobody carries a phone; someone else might want neural implants. someone else might want to live in vice city (either the real version or just a super realistic matrix-sim). ai could help design the economic arrangements that sustain all of this.
-there’s a secondary problem though - even when we have beneficial tech, we may lack the will to diffuse it. waymo and GLP-1s, for example, can save lives (neurosurgeons have compared waymo’s safety results to a treatment so effective that continuing to give patients a placebo would become unethical). and yet evidence of a benefit doesn’t automatically produce the will to act on it.
-the reality described in deep utopia ameliorates this by imagining that our psychology might one day become changeable too. i might want an environment that suits my temperament but i can also go the opposite direction and manipulate myself to become more adventurous or less anxious, in other words, more suited to my environment. the interesting possibility is having more agency over both worlds, external and internal. glps’ effect on appetite already suggests how technology can change the effort involved in pursuing a goal (though again, it is telling that not everyone who *should* be on peptides *are* despite the health benefits). the sci-fi version extends that possibility enormously.
-timing matters. bostrom reminds us that people continue to die while potentially lifesaving advances remain unavailable (he literally says “if nobody builds it, everyone dies” as a hypothetical inversion of yudkowsky/soares’ book).

i’d like ai to make it easier for people to live very different lives, without creating this burden of proof that theirs is the best one.

quote.author: StephDebour
quote.name: Steph Debour
quote.text:
Five years ago, Starlink wasn't on a single ship. Now it's on 66,866. That's more ships than every provider had combined back then.

Before Starlink, if you were a sailor, your internet came from Inmarsat. An unlimited plan cost €3,259 a month for 2 Mbps, and the whole crew had to share it.

Then Starlink showed up in 2022 at US$5,000 a month for up to 350 Mbps. In 2027, a plan that covers an ullimited whole cargo ship comes in at US$4,650.

OneWeb, the closest rival in low orbit, is on 1,662 ships. Its cheapest unlimited plan is about US$7,400 a month, and it maxes out at 30 Mbps.

Market share at sea, by revenue:
2021: Inmarsat almost a third, Starlink 0%
2024: Starlink 39%, the biggest

To be fair, Inmarsat and OneWeb guarantee a minimum speed and Starlink doesn't. Some fleets still pay extra for that.

Zero to number one in four years, and still the cheaper option. That's hard to compete with.

Elon is describing the core of how neural nets (and intelligence) work: semantic compression means squeezing raw data into a compact internal model of meaning, while correlation means learning the mapping from that model to useful outputs. 

In the example, a car’s video + sensor bitstream gets compressed into an understanding of the scene, then directly correlated to the exact driving commands needed. It’s efficient single-path learning, not doing two separate things at once.

quote.author: XFreeze
quote.name: X Freeze
quote.text:
Starlink is rapidly expanding across Africa, and it has already reached more than half the continent

What started in Nigeria in 2023 has now grown into a satellite internet network spanning West, East, Central and Southern Africa

The scale today:

• 30 of Africa's 54 countries listed as having Starlink service
• 15 more countries on the upcoming launch list
• Expanding into remote regions where traditional broadband infrastructure is difficult and expensive to build

And the impact goes far beyond connecting homes

In Zambia, Starlink has connected more than 600 healthcare facilities, helping medical workers access digital health systems, remote consultations and essential medical information

In Mozambique, over 300 schools have been connected, giving students and teachers access to online learning in rural communities

Across Africa, Starlink is helping connect:

• Rural homes and underserved communities
• Schools and healthcare facilities
• Farms, businesses and remote industries
• Emergency and disaster response teams
• Government services in hard-to-reach regions

For decades, connecting remote communities meant building expensive infrastructure, laying cables and extending networks over enormous distances

Starlink is changing that

A village, school or hospital no longer has to wait years for fiber infrastructure to reach it before getting access to high-speed internet

All it needs is a Starlink terminal, power and a clear view of the sky

That's what makes satellite connectivity so important for Africa's future

quote.author: SawyerMerritt
quote.name: Sawyer Merritt
quote.text:
SpaceX has agreed to forgo $738 million in U.S. federal broadband subsidies and instead provide free @Starlink hardware to eligible American households.

NTIA: "To ensure that no consumer at a Covered BSL is left behind, the provider (SpaceX) will serve the covered BSLs as this agreement provides. This includes providing customer premises equipment at no cost to new subscribers, so that households at covered BSL do not face the upfront equipment costs. Additionally, the provider’s broadband service will be subject to the same delivery timelines and performance testing requirements applicable to all recipients of BEAD funds."

Under the new agreement, SpaceX would:
• Provide free Starlink hardware to eligible households.
• Guarantee minimum download speeds of 100 Mbps and upload speeds of 20 Mbps.
• Offer a low-cost monthly internet plan.
• Commit to providing service for 10 years.
• Continue to comply with federal performance testing requirements.

The agreement will save American taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars while accelerating high-speed internet access in underserved rural communities.

In exchange, SpaceX would be exempt from most BEAD-related financial audits, procurement requirements and administrative reporting, while remaining subject to network performance testing.

quote.author: mayemusk
quote.name: Maye Musk
quote.text: The first room at the front door was Elon‘s. There was a mattress on the floor. When the young people arrived and were dancing upstairs, I thought the floor was going to collapse so I moved the mattress to the wall. I assumed just the middle would collapse. I put the door money in a shoebox. When I saw it was quite a lot, I fetched a kitchen knife in case someone tried to take it away from me. I was also the coat check girl. When the police arrived after midnight due to complaints about the noise, I answered the door in my pajamas. That night I slept on the mattress on the floor. It was still better than sleeping on the ground in the Kalahari desert with hyenas, lions, snakes or scorpions visiting us. Memories from my childhood made me appreciate a mattress.

quote.author: LisaBritton
quote.name: Lisa Britton
quote.text:
Iceland is considered “the most gender-equal country in the world” but it doesn’t seem “equal” to me… Currently, they have a female President, Prime Minister, the head of every political party is a woman and the majority of cabinet is women. 68.8% of students who graduated college last year were women. This list goes on about how “gender equality” actually seems to mean female dominance today.

Yesterday I spoke with the former First Lady of Iceland. She did seem concerned about the college student stat, but she insisted there was still so much to do to fight for gender equality for women there.

I think it might be time to look at the disadvantages of both sexes when it comes to addressing “gender equality.” No?

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
I've been using @bot to help my fiancée and me plan our wedding, and it honestly feels like we have a hired full-time wedding planner.

Over the last month, it helped us figure out our hotel room block.

It found 15 hotels within 35 minutes of our venue, handled all the email correspondence, and got proposals with the details we needed to decide.

Then it created a comparison sheet with the criteria we cared about and recommended a shortlist.

Once we picked one, it helped us review the contract, negotiated with the hotel, and even signed it (w/ my permission, of course).

The day after we signed,  @bot proactively researched a shortlist of shuttle services and welcome-party venues, with emails already drafted for my review.

I can't imagine planning a wedding without it. It's truly an amazing time to be alive.
